summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain, gastroparesis, functional dyspepsia, anxiety, depression, and PTSD was admitted for an acute flare of epigastric pain and nausea, consistent with prior episodes. She was managed with an established inpatient protocol involving initial NPO status, IV fluids, pain control, and gradual dietary advancement. She initially failed a trial of clear liquids but later tolerated a BRAT diet. During the admission, she developed cellulitis at an IV site on her left hand, which was treated with IV ceftriaxone followed by oral Keflex. Her pain and nausea improved, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her home medications, complete the antibiotic course, and follow up with her PCP and GI specialist.
